original_value: In breakthrough results, Saxton‐Thomason and Balogh‐Morris‐Samotij developed powerful theories of hypergraph containers. In this paper, we explore some consequences of these theories. We use a simple container theorem of Saxton‐Thomason and an entropy‐based framework to deduce container and counting theorems for hereditary properties of k‐colorings of very general objects, which include both vertex‐ and edge‐colorings of general hypergraph sequences as special cases. In the case of sequences of complete graphs, we further derive characterization and transference results for hereditary properties in terms of their stability families and extremal entropy. This covers within a unified framework a great variety of combinatorial structures, some of which had not previously been studied via containers: directed graphs, oriented graphs, tournaments, multigraphs with bounded multiplicity, and multicolored graphs among others. Similar results were recently and independently obtained by Terry.

result.paraphrase: Building on the breakthrough work of Saxton–Thomason and Balogh–Morris–Samotij on hypergraph containers, this paper investigates some consequences of those theories. Using a simple container theorem of Saxton–Thomason together with an entropy-based framework, we prove container and counting theorems for hereditary properties of k-colorings of very general objects, including vertex- and edge-colorings of arbitrary hypergraph sequences as special cases. For sequences of complete graphs, we also obtain characterization and transference results for hereditary properties expressed through their stability families and extremal entropy. This yields a unified treatment of a wide range of combinatorial structures, including directed graphs, oriented graphs, tournaments, multigraphs of bounded multiplicity, and multicolored graphs, among others, some of which had not previously been studied using containers. Similar results were obtained independently and recently by Terry.
